templates.source: Vivotek IB9367-EHT-v2 User Manual (ManualsLib manual/2744629, p.35, p.99): 'The address format is rtsp://<ip address>:<rtsp port>/<RTSP streaming access name for stream1 or stream2>', example 'rtsp://192.168.5.151:554/live1s1.sdp'. Confirmed by Vivotek Support KB 'Unable to get HTTP/RTSP streaming via 3rd party software after upgrading firmware to 0x13 or above' (vivotek.zendesk.com/hc/en-001/articles/900006469063): default access name changed from live.sdp to live1s1.sdp at firmware 0x13+; access name configurable under Configuration > Network > Streaming Protocols > RTSP > Access name for stream 1.

Vivotek Support KB (vivotek.zendesk.com/hc/en-001/articles/900006469063): stream indexing follows live1s<N>.sdp pattern — 'replace s0 with s1, s2, or s3 for stream2, stream3, or stream4 respectively'; stream 2 access name is therefore live1s2.sdp by the documented convention. Confirmed in Vivotek IB9367-EHT-v2 User Manual (ManualsLib manual/2744629): 'URL format rtsp://<ip>:<port>/<access name for stream 1 to 3>'.

notes: Vivotek (vivotek.com, Taiwanese manufacturer) uses user-configurable RTSP access names. Factory defaults changed at firmware 0x13: stream 1 changed from live.sdp to live1s1.sdp, stream 2 from live2.sdp to live1s2.sdp. The naming convention is live1s<N>.sdp where N is the 1-based stream index. Default RTSP port is 554. Access names are configurable under Configuration > Network > Streaming Protocols > RTSP > Access name for stream <N>. Newer firmware (2.2002.x.x+) also supports ONVIF Media2 at /media2/stream.sdp?profile=token (documented in Vivotek Support KB vivotek.zendesk.com/hc/en-001/articles/4952515434649) but this profile-based URL is outside the fixed-template scope of this dataset.
